preamble: Fortition of the lateral approximant [l] to the voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] is best known from Welsh, where inherited and borrowed word-initial *l- became ll [ɬ] (Proto-Celtic *lindos > llyn, Latin liber > llyfr). In West Greenlandic, geminate /l/ is realized as [ɬː].

examples.note: Via Proto-Brythonic *llɨnn; word-initial *l- regularly became [ɬ]. Compare Irish leann 'ale', which keeps [l].
Latin loans with initial l- also show the change (Middle Welsh llyuyr).
When /l/ is geminated it is realized as a voiceless lateral fricative.

sources: Wiktionary (2026). llyn (Welsh, from Proto-Brythonic *llɨnn, from Proto-Celtic *lindos). https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/llyn
